findings.text: The first sentence plainly says what Athena is, so a newcomer can name it right away.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: This one line is the only explanation of why Athena matters. It never says what problem it solves or how it differs from other AI coding tools, so the 'why' is thin.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page is at Athena's own address, but nearly everything below the header describes firstmate, another project. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets one paragraph on it and many screens on something else.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate.

findings.text: A next-step link sits at the top and jumps to a clear Next steps section, so the newcomer knows where to go without scrolling through the study.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The install step assumes you already have a checkout and gives no clone command. It also lists no requirements, such as a Rust toolchain or AI model access.
findings.source: Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh

findings.text: A concrete first command is given, which helps. It doesn't say what the command will do to your repository or what you'll see afterwards.
findings.source: Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog"

findings.text: Key terms (captain, yolo, green, red) are defined before they are used. This makes the firstmate sections easier to follow, though the definition of 'in scope' admits that it has no test for what counts.
Eleven cards (t1 to t11), plus the exit codes 75 and 1, the counter name 'places-held' and claim ids on every sentence, make most of the page reference material. It is too dense for a first visit.
Every statement can be traced to a claim and its source lines in firstmate, and the page explains how to follow these links. That shows a newcomer the care Athena takes over evidence.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: The page openly says nothing was run and that a first reading missed several paths. That honesty helps trust, but it also tells the newcomer the demo is not proven by running it.
